clue.text: Tool needed to make a cocktail

definitions.meaning: a drink of vodka and orange juice

explanation.surface: Someone wants a particular implement before they can mix a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hand tool for driving screws and a vodka-and-orange-juice drink.

clue.text: Companion always in good humour

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A friend who is never in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the abbreviation for a Companion of Honour, a British honour; EER is the old poetic spelling of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer can mean high spirits or gladness, a state of being in a good mood.

clue.text: Move to Siena from the country

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to relocate to an Italian city from one's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' looks like an instruction to relocate, but it rearranges the letters of TO SIENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation, one example of a country.

clue.text: Abscond from French bivouac

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a bivouac is a temporary encampment, a camp

explanation.surface: Running away from a military encampment in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, just as one who absconds slips away.

clue.text: Taking advantage is grand

definitions.meaning: grand in the sense of impressive and stately

explanation.surface: Exploiting someone turns out to be splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing on a person is presuming on their kindness, and an imposing building is impressive in size and dignity.

clue.text: Incident featured in letter and poem

annotationWithheld.why: 'Incident featured in letter and poem' (7): the only parse is the letter PSI inside the poem EPODE, which gives EPSIODE, not EPISODE; no reading of 'letter' supplies IS, and no source gives the setter's parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Incident featured in letter and poem

clue.text: He produces the finest poetic works around mid- April

definitions.text: He produces the finest poetic works around mid- April

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are placed round the letter taken from April
works is read as a verb, the letters of the two words being worked into a new order
mid- picks out the central letter of the word April

explanation.surface: A poet who turns out superb verse in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' is a verb here, telling us to rework the letters, and 'around' wraps them round the middle letter of 'April'. Read whole, the clue also describes someone who settles only for the best.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler who will settle only for flawless results is exactly someone who produces the finest work.

clue.text: See two articles with hatred

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
the first article is the grammatical article a
the second article is an item or object, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone notices a pair of objects and detests them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' plays on two senses: the grammatical article A and an article meaning an object, a THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or disgust, a strong form of hatred.

clue.text: Labouring whilst imprisoned

definitions.meaning: in labour, giving birth (the old word for childbirth confinement)

explanation.surface: A woman goes into labour while she is in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Confinement is an old word for the period of childbirth, so a woman in labour is in confinement; 'whilst' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a woman giving birth (old-fashioned confinement) and a prisoner held under lock and key.

clue.text: Calm time for the occasion

parts.note: even can mean calm and steady, as in an even temper

explanation.surface: A quiet moment suits a special happening.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or notable occurrence, a synonym of occasion.

clue.text: Sign to receive grain from Italian isle

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is cereal grain

explanation.surface: Someone signs for a shipment of wheat sent from an island off Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' tells us the island takes the grain on board, here at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is one of the twelve zodiac signs, the goat.

clue.text: Freemason upset by Tom, Dick or Harry!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the word Freemason are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A member of a secret fraternity is annoyed by three ordinary men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Dick or Harry' are three example given names, so the definition is by example, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick and Harry are all first names, given names that come before a surname.

clue.text: Top garden party

parts.note: a garden is outdoors, outside, so it suggests out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A garden party that surpasses all others.
explanation.walkthrough: A garden party is an outdoor do, so 'garden' gives OUT and 'party' DO; 'Top' is a verb, meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is to beat or surpass them, the same as to outdo them.

clue.text: Nonchalant part-time employee

definitions.meaning: a worker hired on an irregular, temporary basis

explanation.surface: A temp who takes the job lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relaxed and offhand, and as a noun it names an occasional, irregular worker.

clue.text: Shady men regrouped in south London

indicators.note: regrouped says the letters of shady men are gathered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Suspicious characters gather again in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a district in south London, so 'south London' defines it as a place there; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydenham is a district in the London borough of Lewisham, an area of south London.

clue.text: Peacekeepers have conviction, despite lack of faith

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces come from the United Nations
a conviction is a firmly held belief

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops hold firm views even though they lack religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' looks like a court verdict but here is a firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is the absence of religious belief, a want of faith.

clue.text: Persistent objections about to be produced

indicators.note: about tells us the word for objections is turned round

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
born means brought forth, produced

explanation.surface: Repeated complaints are about to be brought forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' before 'to be produced', but it is the reversal signal; BUTS for objections comes from the phrase 'no ifs or buts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is dogged and unyielding, which is a sense of persistent.

clue.text: Show how it can die in dire distress

indicators.note: in dire distress says the words it can die are in a bad state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An explanation of how something might perish when suffering badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or make known, a synonym of show.

clue.text: Keep using unusual dialect

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of dialect are put in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Someone speaks with an odd regional accent to hold on to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: the strongest tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a castle's fortified stronghold, as is a citadel.

clue.text: Keep talking? That's right!

definitions.meaning: to talk on and on tediously

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether to continue speaking and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to talk at length about something, and as an exclamation it means spot on or exactly correct.

clue.text: Able to accommodate superior detective, it's heard

indicators.note: to accommodate says the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: taken as written
U stands for upper-class, superior
DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: Someone capable makes room for a senior investigator, and it is noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class (superior) usage; DI is a British Detective Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Something audible can be caught by the ear, so it is capable of being heard.

clue.text: Horny growth covering each membrane

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second, covering it

parts.note: a corn is a hard, horny growth of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A hardened lump of skin spreads over a thin tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' places CORN above EA in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent layer at the front of the eye, a type of membrane.

clue.text: Number ten retired from this group

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so ten is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Player number ten has quit the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests a footballer quitting, but it means drawn back, the reversal signal. A nonet is a group of nine, so 'this group' gives the definition its place in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine musicians or a composition for them, a musical group.

clue.text: A carpet depicting an avenue in flower

indicators.note: in says the road is placed inside the word for flower

parts.note: a bloom is a flower
an avenue is a road

explanation.surface: A rug shows a tree-lined street in blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flower' reads like blossoming, but 'in' is the container signal splitting the flower word; 'depicting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven on a wide loom in one seamless width.

clue.text: Some devout religionists are bizarre

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few pious believers behave strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'are' to fit the surface; OUTRE is borrowed from French, meaning eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional and eccentric, so it is a synonym of bizarre.

clue.text: Get up depressed and resign

parts.note: to get up is to stand
down means low in spirits, depressed

explanation.surface: Someone rises feeling glum and quits the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to withdraw from a post, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Graduate with style joins the staff

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
ton means fashionable style

explanation.surface: A new graduate with flair is hired by the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the staff' looks like the workforce but means a stick; TON is an old word for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, such as one used by a conductor.

clue.text: Secrete a French writer in royal house

parts.note: to secrete is to hide, as one plants something
taken as written
Jean Genet was a French novelist and playwright

explanation.surface: Smuggling a Parisian author into a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secrete' looks like produce a fluid but means hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the English ruling dynasty from Henry II to Richard III.
